cards.title: SNP definability of CSPs in NP
cards.formal: Which constraint satisfaction problems in NP admit an exact definition in SNP? The source states this as a classification direction without prescribing a structural criterion. A known equivalent description by reducts of finitely bounded structures is recorded below, but it does not by itself identify what further classification the historical question seeks.
cards.why: This direction seeks to explain when general NP verification for a CSP can be replaced by finitely many guessed relations and universal local checks. The known forbidden-pattern reformulation connects syntax to infinite templates. The intended further classification must be specified before its exact significance and completion criterion can be assessed.
cards.status_note: The 2008 source poses a broad classification direction. The checked 2021/January 2026 monograph and July 2026 LICS paper give an exact normal form and finite-pattern representation, but do not explicitly identify that reformulation as resolving this historical question. The intended substantive criterion beyond the known equivalence has not been specified, so neither resolved status nor a precise remaining open theorem is certified.

sentences: The historical source asks which NP constraint satisfaction problems have an exact SNP definition.
SNP guesses fixed-arity relations on the input and checks a fixed universal first-order condition.
Known results translate such CSPs exactly into reducts of structures with finitely many forbidden induced patterns.
The checked sources do not identify that reformulation as resolving the intended broader classification direction.
The card remains pending until a substantive criterion beyond the known equivalence is specified.

cards.definitions:
A finite relational signature \(\tau\) is a finite list of relation symbols of fixed positive integer arities. A template \(\Gamma\) interprets these symbols as relations on a nonempty domain, which may be finite or infinite. A finite input structure \(I\) has domain \([n]\), \(n\geq0\), and an explicit list of tuples for each symbol. A homomorphism \(h:I\to\Gamma\) preserves all listed positive relation tuples; it need not be injective or preserve absence of tuples. The language \(\operatorname{CSP}(\Gamma)\) accepts exactly such inputs with a homomorphism. Repeated coordinates and isolated elements are allowed, and the empty structure maps to every template.

Encode \(n\) in unary and then each relation’s unary list length followed by binary tuple indices, in signature order, with delimiters. Let \(L\) be total bit length; invalid encodings are rejected. Membership in NP means that there is a deterministic Turing verifier and a polynomial \(p\) such that a valid input is accepted exactly when it has a binary certificate of length at most \(p(L)\) accepted by the verifier within \(p(L)\) bit steps. The template and signature are fixed; no effective presentation or homomorphism oracle for the infinite domain is an input. No complexity separation is assumed.

An SNP sentence over the input signature \(\tau\) has form
\[\Phi=\exists S_1\cdots\exists S_t\ \forall x_1\cdots\forall x_q\ \psi,\]
where the \(S_j\) are fresh relation symbols of fixed finite positive arities and \(\psi\) is a quantifier-free first-order formula using input relations, the new relations, equality, Boolean connectives and the displayed individual variables. Truth constants are allowed. The formula, the numbers \(t,q\) and all arities are fixed independently of input size. On \(I\), the existential quantifiers choose relations on the same domain \([n]\); the universal quantifiers range over all tuples of input elements. There is no built-in order, arithmetic, constant naming input elements, or auxiliary larger universe. General arities are allowed: SNP is not restricted to unary second-order predicates. The empty-domain convention is the usual one for universal sentences, consistent with accepting the empty CSP input.

Exact SNP definability means \(I\models\Phi\) if and only if \(I\to\Gamma\) for every finite \(\tau\)-structure \(I\). There is no reduction or change of input signature hidden in this equivalence. A fixed SNP sentence has polynomial-size guessed relation tables and polynomially many universal tuples to check, so it always defines an NP problem. Arbitrary existential second-order sentences may contain alternating first-order quantifiers; restricting that part to a universal block is the additional requirement here.

For the known structural reformulation, a finite-signature structure \(C\) is finitely bounded if a finite list \(\mathcal N\) of finite structures in its signature satisfies
\[D\text{ embeds into }C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{no }N\in\mathcal N\text{ embeds into }D\]
for every finite \(D\). An embedding is an injective map preserving both relation membership and nonmembership, so the bounds are forbidden induced patterns. The age of \(C\) is the class of its finite induced substructures up to isomorphism. For signatures \(\tau\subseteq\sigma\), the reduct \(C\upharpoonright\tau\) forgets the symbols in \(\sigma\setminus\tau\) and keeps the same domain and remaining relations. No homogeneity or omega-categoricity is required. The representing reduct may differ from the original template; equality of their finite-instance CSPs is what matters.

The source classification direction concerns templates, or equivalently their finite-instance CSP classes. It does not specify an algorithm receiving finite descriptions of infinite structures. A countable representative suffices: choose one solution image for each satisfiable finite instance and take the induced substructure on their countable union.
cards.answer_criterion: A precise completion criterion still requires selecting the additional structural characterization or effectiveness requirement intended beyond the known logical-to-forbidden-pattern representation. The source does not prescribe such a requirement. Merely restating SNP definability by existence of a finite universal expansion is insufficient to certify that this historical research direction is resolved; no particular stronger criterion is selected here.

context_blocks.text:
The following exact representation theorem is known:
\[\chi_{\mathrm{SNP}}(\tau,\Gamma)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists\sigma\supseteq\tau\ \exists C\ \bigl[C\text{ is countable and finitely bounded over finite }\sigma\ \land\ \operatorname{CSP}(\Gamma)=\operatorname{CSP}(C\upharpoonright\tau)\bigr].\]
This equivalence is a structural reformulation of SNP definability, not a separately stated solution of the historical classification question. The equality is on all finite structures in the original signature. The LICS 2026 introduction explicitly identifies this class correspondence. It allows arbitrary finite bounds and auxiliary relations; homogeneity is not an extra condition.

For the forward direction, every CSP is closed under inverse homomorphisms and under disjoint unions. The monograph shows that an SNP sentence defining such a class can be chosen monotone and connected. Monotone means that input relations occur only negatively in clauses; connected means that each clause’s variables are connected through its negative relation literals. These are normal-form transformations of the given problem, not changes to the accepted inputs.

Consider all finite expanded structures satisfying the universal first-order part of that connected sentence. This class is closed under induced substructures, and connectedness makes it closed under disjoint unions. The disjoint union of one representative of each finite isomorphism type is therefore a countable structure whose age is exactly this class. Since the universal formula mentions only finitely many variables, its failures have finitely many minimal finite induced patterns, giving a finite bound list. Forgetting the guessed relations produces a template with exactly the original CSP.

Conversely, a CSP of a reduct of a finitely bounded structure is described in SNP by guessing equality classes for variables and the missing relational pattern on their prospective values. Universal clauses enforce congruence, the original positive constraints and avoidance of the finitely many forbidden induced patterns. The resulting quotient pattern embeds into the representing structure precisely when those constraints pass. This supplies finite universal certificates even when the domain of the representing template is infinite.

The representation concerns some template with the same CSP. It does not assert that the particular supplied template has a finitely bounded expansion, nor provide a uniform recognition algorithm for arbitrary infinite presentations. The 2008 question specifies neither of these stronger requirements. Choosing one, or choosing a particular algebraic invariant, would supply a new completion target rather than merely unpack its notation.

The monograph’s integer-successor example shows why omega-categoricity must not be added to this answer. Its CSP is definable in connected monotone SNP, but cannot be represented by an omega-categorical template with the same accepted finite structures. Thus SNP definability and the symmetry assumptions of infinite-domain dichotomy conjectures are distinct.

The 2026 paper separately studies extensional SNP and CSPs of finitely bounded structures before forgetting relations. These are distinct settings. Its discussion supplies the exact representation theorem above, but does not explicitly identify it as a resolution of the 2008 classification question. The distinction between a structural reformulation and the intended new classification therefore remains material.

statement_review.remaining_issue: The source asks which NP CSPs are SNP-definable, but gives no proposed structural invariant or required form of classification. Exact representation by reducts of finitely bounded structures is already known through a translation of the universal existential expansion; no checked later source identifies that reformulation as resolving the historical question. A completion criterion must specify what substantive new invariant or effectiveness requirement is sought beyond this known equivalence. Selecting one would add a target absent from the source.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Inactive records are archived outside the catalogue, exports and editorial work. Their content, stable IDs and reasons are retained; imports cannot reactivate them. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Inactive cards, including resolved records, are archived outside the ranking without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
